turnaround_reason: Coty collapsed to a sub-$3 stock as soft mass beauty, a slowing fragrance cycle, and a heavy debt load overwhelmed the story; it withdrew FY26 guidance in early 2026. It is recovering (+10.6% over 30d) as JAB-backed management sells non-core assets and deleverages, but debt remains the dominant risk.
bullish_points: Active deleveraging: net debt cut ~$840M YoY to ~$2.9B (leverage ~3.4x), aided by monetizing the Wella stake for $750M and selling the Gucci Beauty license back to Kering for $400M+
Q4 FY26 results came in ahead of expectations — an 'encouraging step' in execution consistency per management
Deep-value optics: price/book ~0.86, EV/EBITDA ~7.7, forward P/E ~11.4 on a global prestige-fragrance franchise
Some open-market insider buying (an officer/director bought ~$200k at $2.41; CFO added a small clip)
Strong gross margins (~63%) and positive FCF (~$363M) give the deleveraging plan runway
bearish_points: Debt is still the story: $3.3B total debt, D/E ~97.5%, and a weak current ratio of 0.755 — little margin for error
Management withdrew FY26 guidance and declined to issue FY27 guidance, citing an early-stage restructuring — low visibility
Operating margin negative (-2.4%) and profit margin -10.4%; the core Consumer Beauty segment remains under pressure
Sub-$3 share price and JAB majority control (majority owner) limit float and leave minority holders as price-takers
Turnaround depends on a still-uncertain prestige-fragrance cycle and continued asset sales to hit leverage targets
catalyst: Further debt reduction milestones and evidence the prestige fragrance business is reaccelerating; eventual reinstatement of guidance
suggested_trade: Pass for now / tiny speculative spot only. Wait for management to reinstate guidance and show a leverage path below 3x before sizing up
key_risk: Fragrance demand softens while high fixed debt costs eat the equity — a levered value trap if deleveraging stalls
would_skip_if: Leverage stops falling, another guidance withdrawal, or Consumer Beauty revenue keeps declining
